IND320 Project P2¶

Author: Robin Torjussen Egede
Streamlit P2 page - P1 page
Repo & P2 branch

(Streamlit does not support changing branch for the online served page, hence the split)

Log¶

Before changing anything I:

  • Made a snapshot branch of P1.
  • Reorganised the loose files into the CA1 folder.
  • Created a separate work-p2 branch so that peer-review changes do not clutter main.
  • Set up a new online streamlit app linked to the new branch.

Did the local cassandra + spark setup. The notebook starts the container automatically if it is stopped.
Spark caused the most friction: the original Python 3.14/JDK combination did not work.
I changed to Python 3.12, installed OpenJDK 17 and explicitly set JAVA_HOME before importing PySpark.

MongoDB:
The connection string and ENTSO-E token are read through SecretManager (created in P1).
No credentials are stored in the notebook or on git.

API data: API results are cached as local parquet files under data/cache.
Rerunning the notebook does not re-query the api.
Bool flags REFRESH_NVE and REFRESH_ENTSOE force a fresh fetch if needed.

NVE:
The NVE Magasinstatistikk data are now fetched directly from HentOffentligData.
Otherwise more or less the same as P1.

ENTSOE:
Chose documentType = A11, as this was listed as Cross-Border Physical Flows.
Fetched Area Y EIC codes from https://www.entsoe.eu/data/energy-identification-codes-eic/eic-approved-codes (data/Y_eicCodes.csv).
Chose code 10YNO-0--------C for Norway. Visually inspected the web-gui for connected countries.
Concluded the neighbours are: SE, FI, NL, GB, DK, DE.

Every neighbouring country is queried in both directions (due to values being positive only):

  • NO -> neighbour for exports
  • neighbour -> NO for imports.

The A11 responses contain mixed time resolutions.
The parser stores the resolution and converts each observation to hours before converting to Wh.
The rows are written to Cassandra with Spark, read back through Spark SQL.

Finally, rows are inserted into MongoDB in chunks.

Streamlit:
Removed the dummy page and reorganised the app into:

  • Home
  • Reservoir table
  • Reservoir plot
  • Cross-border flows

The reservoir pages share a cached NVE loader,
and the session-state interval controlled by the slider on the plot page.
Radio buttons for EL, NO or VASS.
The cross-border page uses two columns with radios for desired connection and year selector on the left.
Pill buttons for month and a line plot on the right.
Expander below for the required brief data source doc.

I figured I would give AI driven dev a shot.
Therefor I prototyped all of the above (except for the new streamlit stuff),
and let the agent finish the work. Lastly I did the final polish myself before delivery.

AI usage¶

Used as "fancy auto-complete" in-line suggestions, docstring & in-line comment drafts, plotting drafts.
All logic is my own.
I let a fully autonomous agent take my "80%"-prototype to "fully developed".

def require_columns(
    frame: pd.DataFrame,
    required: tuple[str, ...] | list[str],
    source: str,
) -> None:
    """Raise a readable error when a cache or API table is incomplete."""
    missing = sorted(set(required) - set(frame.columns))
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"{source} is missing columns: {', '.join(missing)}")

# Cassandra connection and Spark-Cassandra round-trip test
KEYSPACE = "ind320"
TEST_TABLE = "connection_test"

cluster = Cluster(["localhost"], port=9042)
session = cluster.connect()
session.execute(
    f"""
    CREATE KEYSPACE IF NOT EXISTS {KEYSPACE}
    WITH REPLICATION = {{'class': 'SimpleStrategy', 'replication_factor': 1}}
    """
)
session.set_keyspace(KEYSPACE)

# Build a tiny table, cassandra, and read it back with Spark.
# This is "proof" that both access paths work before the real data is loaded.
session.execute(f"DROP TABLE IF EXISTS {TEST_TABLE}")
session.execute(
    f"""
    CREATE TABLE {TEST_TABLE} (
        id TIMEUUID PRIMARY KEY,
        name TEXT,
        value DOUBLE,
        created_at TIMESTAMP
    )
    """
)

# Insert
for name, value in [("a", 1.2), ("b", 3.4), ("c", 5.6)]:
    session.execute(
        f"INSERT INTO {TEST_TABLE} (id, name, value, created_at) "
        f"VALUES (now(), '{name}', {value}, currentTimestamp())"
    )

print(f"Cassandra release: {session.execute('SELECT release_version FROM system.local').one().release_version}")
print("Rows written with CQL:")
for row in session.execute(f"SELECT name, value FROM {TEST_TABLE}"):
    print(f"  {row.name}: {row.value}")

# Spark readback
test_sdf = (
    spark.read.format("org.apache.spark.sql.cassandra")
    .options(table=TEST_TABLE, keyspace=KEYSPACE)
    .load()
)
print("Same table read back through Spark:")
test_sdf.show(truncate=False)

# The test table is not needed for the project data.
session.execute(f"DROP TABLE {TEST_TABLE}")

NVE Magasinstatistikk API¶

P1 read a local reservoirs.csv.
The same public endpoint is now called directly.
omrType contains the three area types (EL, NO, VASS) and omrnr is the area number (0-5).
The keys are renamed to the English names used in P1 so that the plotting code remains comparable.

The cleaned response is cached as data/cache/magasinstatistikk.parquet.
Later runs load that file instead of calling the API.
Set REFRESH_NVE = True to force a new download.

In [6]:
# The NVE rename/type logic lives in src/utils/magasin.py so the notebook and
# the Streamlit app share one implementation.
MAGASIN_CACHE = PARQUET_CACHE
MAGASIN_COLUMNS = REQUIRED_COLUMNS
REFRESH_NVE = False


def load_magasinstatistikk() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Load the NVE data from the parquet cache or fetch and cache it."""
    if MAGASIN_CACHE.exists() and not REFRESH_NVE:
        frame = pd.read_parquet(MAGASIN_CACHE)
        require_columns(frame, MAGASIN_COLUMNS, "NVE cache")
        print(
            f"Loaded {len(frame):,} rows from cache: "
            f"{MAGASIN_CACHE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}"
        )
        return frame.sort_values("date").reset_index(drop=True)

    frame = fetch_magasinstatistikk()
    frame.to_parquet(MAGASIN_CACHE, index=False)
    print(
        f"Fetched {len(frame):,} rows from the API and cached them in "
        f"{MAGASIN_CACHE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}"
    )
    return frame


df_mag = load_magasinstatistikk()

# Display some basic info
print(f"Shape of the API data: {df_mag.shape}")
print(f"Area types: {sorted(df_mag['area_type'].unique())}")
print(
    "Area numbers: "
    f"{sorted(int(value) for value in df_mag['area_number'].unique())}"
)
print(f"Date range: {df_mag['date'].min().date()} to {df_mag['date'].max().date()}")
display(df_mag.head())

# A compact column summary, equivalent to the P1 sanity-check cell.
def describe_column(name: str) -> str:
    """Return a one-line type/range summary for a Magasinstatistikk column."""
    series = df_mag[name]
    if pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(series):
        return f"{name} [{series.dtype}]: {series.min()} -> {series.max()}"
    if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(series):
        return (
            f"{name} [{series.dtype}]: min={series.min():.3f}, "
            f"max={series.max():.3f}, mean={series.mean():.3f}"
        )
    return f"{name} [{series.dtype}]: {', '.join(map(str, series.unique()[:10]))}"


for column in df_mag.columns:
    print(describe_column(column))

Recreated P1 plots¶

The first figure mirrors the P1 "one panel per measurement" plot.
The second figure is the normalised per-area plot:

  • each numeric column is scaled to [0, 1] within its area number.
  • each area_type gets its own line style.

# Figure 2: normalise every numeric measurement within each area number.
# Normalisation is done separately per area so that the six subplots are
# comparable even though the absolute reservoir sizes differ.

plot_df = df_mag.copy()
plot_df = plot_df.drop(columns=["iso_year", "iso_week", "next_publication_date"])

# Fetch numeric columns
numeric_cols = [
    c
    for c in plot_df.select_dtypes(include="number").columns
    if c != "area_number"
]

# Normalize values
for area_number in sorted(plot_df["area_number"].unique()):
    
    mask = plot_df["area_number"] == area_number
    
    for column in numeric_cols:
        
        area_values = plot_df.loc[mask, column]
        value_range = area_values.max() - area_values.min()
        
        if value_range == 0:
            plot_df.loc[mask, column] = 1.0
        else:
            plot_df.loc[mask, column] = (area_values - area_values.min()) / value_range

# Integer codes give a stable index into the line-style list.
area_type_codes = {
    name: code
    for code, name in enumerate(sorted(plot_df["area_type"].unique()))
}
plot_df["area_type_code"] = plot_df["area_type"].map(area_type_codes)
line_styles = ["-", "--", "-."]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(
    len(sorted(plot_df["area_number"].unique())),
    1,
    figsize=(22, 24),
    sharex=True,
)

for ax, area_number in zip(axes, sorted(plot_df["area_number"].unique())):
    
    area_data = plot_df[plot_df["area_number"] == area_number]
    ax.set_title(f"Relative values for area {area_number}")

    for area_type, code in area_type_codes.items():
        
        type_data = area_data[area_data["area_type"] == area_type]
        
        for column in numeric_cols:
            ax.plot(
                type_data["date"],
                type_data[column],
                label=f"{column} ({area_type})",
                linestyle=line_styles[code % len(line_styles)],
                linewidth=0.8,
            )

    ax.set_ylabel("Relative value")
    ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.005, 1), fontsize=8)

fig.suptitle("Magasinstatistikk: normalised measurements per area (API data)", y=0.995)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

ENTSO-E cross-border transfer data¶

For cross-border physical flows the Norway control area is 10YNO-0--------C.

The API is queried in both directions for each neighbour:

  • in_Domain = neighbour, out_Domain = NO -> export from Norway
  • in_Domain = NO, out_Domain = neighbour -> import to Norway

ENTSO-E defines out_Domain as the area the energy comes from and in_Domain as the area it flows into.
The quantity is non-negative, so the direction is encoded in the domain order.

The parsed two-year table is cached as data/cache/entsoe_flows.parquet.
Re-runs load the cache instead of repeating the HTTP requests.
Set REFRESH_ENTSOE = True to fetch a new window.

In [10]:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EICAreaCode:
    """A compact view of one row in the ENTSO-E EIC code list."""

    eic_code: str
    display_name: str
    name: str


def clean_text(value: Any) -> str:
    """Return a stripped string, or an empty string for missing values."""
    
    if pd.isna(value):
        return ""
    
    return str(value).strip()


def load_eic_codes(path: Path) -> list[EICAreaCode]:
    """Read the EIC CSV and return only the fields used by the notebook."""
    
    frame = pd.read_csv(path, sep=";", encoding="utf-8-sig")
    
    require_columns(
        frame,
        ("EicCode", "EicDisplayName", "EicLongName"),
        "EIC code list",
    )

    return [
        EICAreaCode(
            eic_code=clean_text(row["EicCode"]),
            display_name=clean_text(row["EicDisplayName"]),
            name=clean_text(row["EicLongName"]),
        )
        for _, row in frame.iterrows()
    ]


eic_path = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "Y_eicCodes.csv"
eic_objects = load_eic_codes(eic_path)

norwegian_areas = [e for e in eic_objects if e.eic_code.startswith("10YNO")]

country_areas = [
    e
    for e in eic_objects
    if e.eic_code.startswith("10Y") and len(e.display_name) == 2
]

NO_CODE = "10YNO-0--------C"  # Norway control area used by the A11 endpoint
NEIGHBOURS = ["SE", "FI", "NL", "GB", "DK", "DE"]

# Map display name -> EIC code and fail loudly if the CSV changes.
country_codes = {area.display_name: area.eic_code for area in country_areas}
missing_neighbours = sorted(set(NEIGHBOURS) - set(country_codes))

if missing_neighbours:
    raise ValueError(
        "Missing EIC codes for: " + ", ".join(missing_neighbours)
    )
    
border_codes = {country: country_codes[country] for country in NEIGHBOURS}

print(f"Loaded {len(eic_objects)} EIC records\n")

print("Norwegian areas:")
for area in norwegian_areas:
    print(f"  {area.eic_code}  {area.display_name:4s}  {area.name}")

print("\nNeighbour codes used:")
for country, code in border_codes.items():
    print(f"  {country}: {code}")

In [11]:
ENTSOE_API = "https://web-api.tp.entsoe.eu/api?"

# The start/end of the requested window:
# exactly two years back from today, normalised to midnight UTC.

END_DATE = pd.Timestamp.now().normalize()
START_DATE = END_DATE - pd.DateOffset(years=2)
print(f"Requested window: {START_DATE} -> {END_DATE}")


def fetch_entsoe_roots(
    start: pd.Timestamp,
    end: pd.Timestamp,
    in_domain: str,
    out_domain: str,
) -> list[ET.Element]:
    """
    Fetch A11 data for one domain pair, splitting into <= 1-year chunks.

    The Transparency Platform limits the length of a single query, so the
    interval is walked one year at a time. A response without a
    Publication_MarketDocument (for example an Acknowledgement_MarketDocument
    saying "no matching data") is skipped and reported.
    """
    roots: list[ET.Element] = []
    cursor = start

    while cursor < end:
        
        chunk_end = min(cursor + pd.DateOffset(years=1), end)
        
        params = {
            "securityToken": entsoe_token,
            "documentType": "A11",  # Aggregated energy data report
            "in_Domain": in_domain,
            "out_Domain": out_domain,
            "periodStart": cursor.strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M"),
            "periodEnd": chunk_end.strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M"),
        }

        response = requests.get(ENTSOE_API, params=params, timeout=120)
        
        if response.ok and "Publication_MarketDocument" in response.text:
            roots.append(ET.fromstring(response.content))
        else:
            print(
                f"  no publication data for {in_domain} -> {out_domain} "
                f"({cursor.date()} to {chunk_end.date()}, HTTP {response.status_code})"
            )

        cursor = chunk_end

    return roots


# Resolution strings map to the duration of one observation in hours. The
# energy of a point is quantity (MW) multiplied by this value.
RESOLUTION_HOURS = {
    "PT15M": 0.25,
    "PT30M": 0.5,
    "PT60M": 1.0,
    "P1D": 24.0,
}


def parse_entsoe_roots(
    roots: list[ET.Element],
    border: str,
    direction: str,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Flatten ENTSO-E TimeSeries/Period/Point XML into a tabular DataFrame.

    The nested structure is: TimeSeries -> Period -> Point. Position is
    1-based within the period, so the timestamp of a point is
    period_start + resolution * (position - 1).
    """
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    for root in roots:
        for series in root.findall(".//{*}TimeSeries"):
            
            unit_element = series.find("{*}quantity_Measure_Unit.name")
            unit = unit_element.text if unit_element is not None else None

            for period in series.findall("{*}Period"):
                
                start_element = period.find("{*}timeInterval/{*}start")
                resolution_element = period.find("{*}resolution")
                
                if start_element is None or resolution_element is None:
                    continue

                period_start = pd.to_datetime(start_element.text)
                
                if period_start.tzinfo is not None:
                    period_start = (
                        period_start.tz_convert("UTC").tz_localize(None)
                    )

                resolution = resolution_element.text
                hours = RESOLUTION_HOURS.get(resolution)
                
                if hours is None:
                    hours = pd.Timedelta(resolution).total_seconds() / 3600.0

                for point in period.findall("{*}Point"):
                    
                    position_element = point.find("{*}position")
                    quantity_element = point.find("{*}quantity")
                    
                    if position_element is None or quantity_element is None:
                        continue

                    timestamp = period_start + pd.Timedelta(hours=hours) * (
                        int(position_element.text) - 1
                    )
                    
                    rows.append(
                        {
                            "border": border,
                            "direction": direction,
                            "timestamp": timestamp,
                            "quantity": float(quantity_element.text),
                            "hours": hours,
                            "unit": unit,
                        }
                    )

    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Requested window: 2024-10-20 00:00:00 -> 2026-10-20 00:00:00
In [12]:
# ENTSO-E data are cached as a parquet file for the same reason as the NVE
# data: a normal notebook run should not depend on network access or on the
# API rate limit. Set REFRESH_ENTSOE = True (or delete the file) to fetch a
# fresh two-year window.

FLOW_COLUMNS = ("border", "direction", "timestamp", "quantity", "hours", "unit")
ENTS0E_CACHE = CACHE_DIR / "entsoe_flows.parquet"
REFRESH_ENTSOE = False


def fetch_all_entsoe(start: pd.Timestamp, end: pd.Timestamp) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fetch both directions for every neighbour and return one tidy table."""
    flow_frames: list[pd.DataFrame] = []

    # This is 2 requests per border per year (normally 24 HTTP calls). The loop
    # prints a short line so the notebook output documents what was retrieved.
    for border in NEIGHBOURS:
        neighbour_code = border_codes[border]

        for direction, in_code, out_code in [
            # out_Domain is the source and in_Domain is the destination.
            ("Export", neighbour_code, NO_CODE),
            ("Import", NO_CODE, neighbour_code),
        ]:
            print(f"{border} {direction}: {in_code} -> {out_code}")
            
            roots = fetch_entsoe_roots(start, end, in_code, out_code)
            frame = parse_entsoe_roots(roots, border, direction)
            
            print(f"  parsed {len(frame):,} points")
            flow_frames.append(frame)

    frame = pd.concat(flow_frames, ignore_index=True)
    require_columns(frame, FLOW_COLUMNS, "ENTS0E parsed data")

    # Different resolutions can describe the same instant. Keep the last row
    # for each key; the API returns the most detailed/newest series last.
    frame = (
        frame.drop_duplicates(["border", "direction", "timestamp"], keep="last")
        .sort_values(["border", "direction", "timestamp"])
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )

    # The partition key in Cassandra uses the calendar year.
    frame["year"] = frame["timestamp"].dt.year
    return frame


def load_entsoe_flows() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Load the flow table from the parquet cache or fetch and cache it."""
    
    if ENTS0E_CACHE.exists() and not REFRESH_ENTSOE:
        
        frame = pd.read_parquet(ENTS0E_CACHE)
        require_columns(frame, (*FLOW_COLUMNS, "year"), "ENTS0E cache")
        
        print(
            f"Loaded {len(frame):,} flow rows from cache: "
            f"{ENTS0E_CACHE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}"
        )
        
        return frame.sort_values(
            ["border", "direction", "timestamp"]
        ).reset_index(drop=True)

    frame = fetch_all_entsoe(START_DATE, END_DATE)
    frame.to_parquet(ENTS0E_CACHE, index=False)
    
    print(
        f"Cached {len(frame):,} flow rows in "
        f"{ENTS0E_CACHE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}"
    )
    
    return frame


df_flows = load_entsoe_flows()

print(f"\nCombined shape: {df_flows.shape}")
print(
    f"Window in data: {df_flows['timestamp'].min()} -> "
    f"{df_flows['timestamp'].max()}"
)
print(df_flows.groupby(["border", "direction"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0))
display(df_flows.head())

Cassandra storage¶

The data are stored in one table with a composite partition key (border, year)
and clustering columns (direction, timestamp).
Partitioning by border and year keeps each Cassandra partition small(roughly 17k rows for a full year),
while still allowing efficient reads for the plots.

Spark writes the DataFrame directly with the Cassandra connector.
The table is recreated on each full notebook run so the result is reproducible.

In [14]:
FLOW_TABLE = "entsoe_flows"
CASSANDRA_FLOW_COLUMNS = (
    "border",
    "year",
    "direction",
    "ts",
    "quantity",
    "hours",
    "unit",
)

session.execute(f"DROP TABLE IF EXISTS {FLOW_TABLE}")
session.execute(
    f"""
    CREATE TABLE {FLOW_TABLE} (
        border TEXT,
        year INT,
        direction TEXT,
        ts TIMESTAMP,
        quantity DOUBLE,
        hours DOUBLE,
        unit TEXT,
        PRIMARY KEY ((border, year), direction, ts)
    )
    """
)

# Only the columns that exist in the Cassandra schema are sent to Spark.
flow_to_write = (
    df_flows.rename(columns={"timestamp": "ts"})[list(CASSANDRA_FLOW_COLUMNS)].copy()
)

# Ensure nullable-free key columns and plain Python/NumPy types.
flow_to_write["ts"] = pd.to_datetime(flow_to_write["ts"])
flow_to_write["year"] = flow_to_write["year"].astype(int)
flow_to_write["quantity"] = flow_to_write["quantity"].astype(float)
flow_to_write["hours"] = flow_to_write["hours"].astype(float)

flow_sdf = spark.createDataFrame(flow_to_write)

(
    flow_sdf.write.format("org.apache.spark.sql.cassandra")
    .options(table=FLOW_TABLE, keyspace=KEYSPACE)
    .mode("append")
    .save()
)

# Read the table back through Spark to verify the write.
cassandra_sdf = (
    spark.read.format("org.apache.spark.sql.cassandra")
    .options(table=FLOW_TABLE, keyspace=KEYSPACE)
    .load()
)
cassandra_sdf.createOrReplaceTempView("entsoe_flows")

print(f"Rows in Cassandra (Spark count): {cassandra_sdf.count():,}")
cassandra_sdf.groupBy("border", "direction").count().orderBy("border", "direction").show()

Spark extraction and plots¶

The plots use Spark SQL to select only the needed columns and to aggregate energy.
quantity is in MW and hours is the length of each observation, SUM(quantity * hours) / 1e6 gives TWh.

  • Pie chart: total export and import for one connection in one complete year.
  • Line plot: January of a chosen year for one connection, with one line per direction, followed by a version showing every connection and direction.
In [15]:
# User-facing choices for the two required plots.
PIE_BORDER = "SE"
PIE_YEAR = 2025
LINE_BORDER = "SE"
LINE_YEAR = 2025
LINE_MONTH = 1

# --- Pie chart -------------------------------------------------------------
pie_sql = f"""
    SELECT direction,
           ROUND(SUM(quantity * hours) / {MWH_PER_TWH}.0, 3) AS twh
    FROM entsoe_flows
    WHERE border = '{PIE_BORDER}' AND year = {PIE_YEAR}
    GROUP BY direction
    ORDER BY direction DESC
"""

pie_df = spark.sql(pie_sql).toPandas()

print(f"{PIE_BORDER} {PIE_YEAR} totals (TWh):")
display(pie_df)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))
colors = {"Export": "#2a9d8f", "Import": "#e76f51"}
ax.pie(
    pie_df["twh"],
    labels=pie_df["direction"],
    autopct=lambda pct: f"{pct:.1f}%\n({pct / 100 * pie_df['twh'].sum():.2f} TWh)",
    startangle=90,
    colors=[colors.get(d, "#999999") for d in pie_df["direction"]],
    wedgeprops={"edgecolor": "white", "linewidth": 1.5},
)

ax.set_title(
    f"Cross-border transfer, {PIE_BORDER} - {PIE_YEAR}\n"
    f"total {pie_df['twh'].sum():.2f} TWh"
)

ax.axis("equal")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

MongoDB export¶

The same Spark-selected columns are inserted into MongoDB.
If SHOULD_PUSH = True:

  • The collection is dropped and rebuilt on every full run so that repeated notebook executions do not create duplicates.
  • Documents are inserted in chunks to keep each request below the request limits.
In [18]:
SHOULD_PUSH = False  # Set to True to push the flow table to MongoDB

MONGO_DB_NAME = "ind320"
MONGO_COLLECTION_NAME = "entsoe_flows"
MONGO_INSERT_CHUNK_SIZE = 5000

mongo_client = MongoClient(mongo_url, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=20000)
mongo_client.admin.command("ping")
mongo_db = mongo_client[MONGO_DB_NAME]
mongo_collection = mongo_db[MONGO_COLLECTION_NAME]

if SHOULD_PUSH:
    mongo_collection.drop()

    mongo_sql = """
        SELECT border, year, direction, ts AS timestamp, quantity, hours, unit
        FROM entsoe_flows
        ORDER BY border, year, direction, ts
    """
    mongo_pdf = spark.sql(mongo_sql).toPandas()
    mongo_pdf["timestamp"] = pd.to_datetime(mongo_pdf["timestamp"])

    records = mongo_pdf.to_dict("records")
    for start in range(0, len(records), MONGO_INSERT_CHUNK_SIZE):
        mongo_collection.insert_many(
            records[start : start + MONGO_INSERT_CHUNK_SIZE],
            ordered=False,
        )

    # Indexes match the filters used by the Streamlit page: connection + year for
    # the pie chart, and timestamp for the month line plot.
    mongo_collection.create_index([("border", 1), ("year", 1)])
    mongo_collection.create_index([("timestamp", 1)])

print(f"Documents in MongoDB: {mongo_collection.count_documents({}):,}")
print("Sample document:")
display(mongo_collection.find_one({}, {"_id": 0}))
